continuity_scope: Elizabeth Moon, Sheepfarmer's Daughter, first novel of The Deed of Paksenarrion (first printing June 1988). This pass is further limited to the authorized Baen electronic Chapter One recruitment-and-march segment, using the Baen edition record ISBN 978-0-671-65416-0. Later chapters and volumes are excluded.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Baen electronic edition record, ISBN 978-0-671-65416-0; authorized Chapter One text.
Baen product record, trade-paperback ISBN 9781481483469; scope metadata only.
Baen front matter, first printing June 1988 and Book I identity.

coverage_rule: Include the six individually named dramatic persons in the authorized Chapter One recruitment-and-march segment: Paksenarrion, recruiting sergeant Stammel, Corporal Bosk, and recruits Saben, Coben, and Korryn. Military ranks, Duke Phelan's Company, the recruiting system, weapons, places, religions, peoples, magic, and narrative functions are dimensions or terms, not nodes.
omissions: All persons appearing after the Chapter One segment, including later protagonist, antagonist, faction-leader, and supernatural agents.
All of Sheepfarmer's Daughter beyond Chapter One; Divided Allegiance, Oath of Gold, Paladin's Legacy, other Paksworld works, adaptations, and author commentary.
Military units, ranks, institutions, religions/orders, magic, peoples, artifacts, places, and generic recruits as character nodes.
uncertainties: The pass is complete only for the authorized Chapter One segment, not for the entire first novel.
The Baen chapter is an electronic witness; page locators differ across printings, so chapter/scene locators are used.
The segment depicts family coercion, threatened corporal punishment, sexualized taunting, military discipline, and implied future violence. Records are non-graphic and do not infer later harms.
evidence_basis: Baen supplies the licensed electronic front matter, Chapter One, and product metadata. The Chapter One text establishes all included character and relationship claims; Baen's product page establishes the single-novel/trilogy boundary. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, adaptation, or later-story material is used.
